# Decisions: match-online-fixes

From the overnight session of 2026-09-25. The operator is asleep and asked the assistant to decide, record each decision, and use the workflow for the code.

## Decisions

- match-online-001 passed every check (including `full-match`). Its coverage reviewer blocked it on results columns untested through the room, and its general reviewer was stopped before a verdict. This follow-up restores its snapshot (`2a47271`) on its base, so the whole feature is reviewed again.
- It includes the branch → test table that ended the intel review loop, so the next review finds nothing left untested.
- The `ineligible` claim reset can't happen through the room, because a lost type always comes with a duel reservation that resets first. It is documented as covered by the pure module.

## Assumptions

- Everything in `features/match-online/` stands.

## Deferred

- `ruins-online` comes next.

concerns.message: Finding 1 needs a settled draw through the real room. The only draw the headless clients can produce quickly is the mirrored double KO (`brawler(0)`/`brawler(1)` in `seaDuelHarness.test.ts`). The repo keeps that fight out of the parallel integration group on purpose: `vitest.config.ts` HARNESS_FILES and the comment at `tests/integration/seaDuel.test.ts:41` both say it 'wants a quiet machine'. `endings.test.ts` runs in the parallel group (3 forks, maxConcurrency 20), and this machine is shared by several runs. If the new draw-then-cache-then-end test goes there, a late input gets replaced by a repeated or neutral one and one fighter wins. The draw then never happens, and the exact results line fails.
concerns.consequence: The integration check fails some of the time. The worker's own run can pass while the verifier's run on the shared machine fails, which uses up the 3 verification attempts and sends the whole feature back through review again. Fix: put the draw ending in the sequential harness group (add the file to HARNESS_FILES; vitest.config.ts is owned), or use a draw that doesn't depend on timing (see simpler_alternative).

concerns.message: The plan says the room can't produce `ineligible` in a running channel, but that holds only if the room passes every duel to `stepClaim` for its whole life, not just on the tick it's accepted. That includes the 5-second theft-choice window after the fight, when the ledger duel is `ended` but not yet `settled`. `stepClaim` only blocks a start through `reservedBy`. If an ended-but-unsettled duel is left out of `ClaimTickInput.encounters`, the loser can still start a channel. The loser still holds every type, has speed 0, may be inside the circle, and may be holding E. The theft then commits and resets that channel with `ineligible`. I can't see the snapshot's room code from the base commit, so this is unverified, not disproved.
concerns.consequence: docs/architecture.md would state as fact something the room can break, and the new branch table would call `ineligible` covered only by the pure module when the room can in fact reach it. The next reviewer then reopens the loop that finding 4 is meant to close.

concerns.message: The results feed counts `duelsDrawn` from `winner: null`. The match module leaves it to the caller whether a cancellation or a duel frozen at match end counts as a draw (`match/state.ts:182`). The room also returns the players of a cancelled duel 'as a draw' (`settledRole: "draw"` in `rubbings.test.ts:331`). A worker under time pressure could fill the `duelsDrawn` column with the quick, reliable ready-timeout cancellation (autoReady false) instead of a real draw. Finding 1 and the branch table don't say how a cancelled duel or one ended by `duel-ended-without-theft` at match end should be counted.
concerns.consequence: Either `duelsDrawn` gets its 'coverage' from a cancellation, which §12 says ends 'without rewards' and isn't a draw, or cancelled and frozen duels silently inflate the drawn count. The coverage reviewer then blocks again on a column that isn't really tested.

concerns.message: The unit project runs with `environment: "node"`. `apps/web/src/main.ts` builds a Phaser game, so a unit test can't import it without a DOM or canvas. Finding 2 therefore effectively needs the extracted handler. If the `event.repeat` guard stays in main.ts's `addEventListener` wrapper while the extracted function only handles the choice, the test drives a path that never sees `repeat`.
concerns.consequence: The test passes even when the guard is deleted, which is exactly what the finding 4 mutation check should catch. Either the reviewer flags the finding as unfixed, or it passes by mistake.

concerns.message: `ClaimInterruptReason` also has `deadline` (`claim/step.ts:163`), but finding 3 lists only five reasons: moved, released, duel, disconnected and ineligible. If the flow HUD maps every reason to text, including one for `deadline`, that branch is left untested and missing from the branch table.
concerns.consequence: The next coverage review finds one more untested UI branch, and the review loop continues, which is what finding 4 is meant to stop.

concerns.message: Finding 4 asks for a mutation check ('delete on a scratch copy and record the failing test') across about 30 branches: lobby, late join, ready, control start, reveals, five or six resets, four endings, nine columns, seeds, and test-only settings. Some branches are tested only by browser scenarios (for example `full-match`), which take minutes each. Scratch edits in the real worktree also risk being left behind or committed.
concerns.consequence: The worker spends most of its time re-running slow suites and hits the 90-minute stop with a partial table, or commits a leftover scratch deletion. Limit the mutation checks to branches whose covering test isn't obvious, run only the one relevant test file each time, and do it in a throwaway `git worktree` rather than the delivery tree.

challenge.simpler_alternative: Don't put one long scripted test (a mirrored double-KO draw, then a quit, a cache claim, a sail to the final island and a 10-second channel) into the parallel `endings.test.ts`. Split finding 1 across the two test groups the repo already has. (a) Add the settled draw's results line to a test in the sequential harness group: extend `seaDuelHarness.test.ts`'s draw, or add a new file to HARNESS_FILES that uses the short match timing. There the draw runs on a quiet machine, and the match can end by the `deadline` with test-only short timings, so there's no sailing or 10-second channel. (b) Put the cache claim (a quit with rubbings, then a claim from the cache) and a `claim` or `deadline` ending in `endings.test.ts`, where timing doesn't matter. Both tests assert the exact results line for every player. Together with the existing endings, all nine columns are non-zero, and the fragile fight is kept in the group built for it.
challenge.cheap_experiment: After restoring the snapshot, check how `MatchRoom.ts` builds the `encounters` list it passes to `stepClaim`. Does it include duels that are `ended` but not yet `settled` (the theft-choice window)? Then add one short integration test: grapple a full-set holder inside the treasure circle, let them lose while holding E, and during the choice window check that no `claim-started` fires for the loser. If a channel does start, `ineligible` is reachable through the room: the documentation decision is wrong, and the room fix (keep unsettled duels reserved) must come before the branch table. Separately, run the planned draw test 5 times in a row alongside the parallel integration group (`npm run test:integration` in a loop). Any run where the fight doesn't end in a double KO settles where the draw has to live.

   - a **cache claim** (a player quits with rubbings, and another claims one from the cache);

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. Apart from restoring the snapshot, change only what the findings need. Keep the structure, names, every scenario id and every existing test.
- Tests drive input like players do.

## Acceptance

- The restored `match-online` feature meets all of `features/match-online/game-task.md`'s acceptance.
- Findings 1–4 are fixed with the tests they name, and the branch table is in the report.
- `npm ci` then each of the five policy checks passes from a clean checkout, with all browser scenarios. The integration suite stays well inside its time budget (report the duration).

Browser checks: each scenario id appears in exactly one test title as `[scenario:<id>]`. That test, when it passes, attaches exactly one image/png named `screenshot:<id>` (other attachments are fine). The verifier refuses anything else. WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=worker PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_FILE=<tmp>/report.json \
  npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts --reporter=json <spec files>

- Restoring the snapshot fails or touches a path outside the owned paths.
- `npm ci` or an install fails twice for reasons outside the repository (registry, network).

scenarios.description: One browser creates a private match from the landing page; the HUD shows the code, the protocol version, one player and a connected status.
Two browsers join the same private match with their ships in sight of each other; one sails with the keyboard and the other browser's view shows that ship at the new server-authoritative position.
A browser sails its ship around a shoal to an island dock with the keyboard and docks there; the HUD shows the dock and the ship stops at it.
Two browsers in one match with their ships out of sight of each other: neither view lists or draws the other ship until one sails within the sight radius, and it disappears again when it sails away.

One browser opens a practice duel against the dummy, lands a jab and then a keyboard throw (J then K a frame apart); the dummy's health bar and the HUD drop by the move data's damage, and hitboxes can be shown.

Two browsers: one creates a duel, the other joins by its code; after the countdown the first lands a strike on the second, and both views show the same authoritative health, round clock and result, with the connection line showing input delay and corrections.

Two browsers in one match are placed within grapple range; the host sails at the guest and presses J; both see the grapple telegraph, then a three-second countdown and the arena; the duel is decided; the winner returns to the sea with protection shown, and the loser sees a respawn countdown and then their ship at a dock.

Two browsers moored at different islands each hold E and collect a different rubbing type; the host grapples the guest at sea, wins the duel by tapping attack keys, and picks the guest's type within five seconds; the host's HUD shows both types and more gold, the guest's shows the loss.

Two browsers: the host starts a private match from the lobby, both see the ready countdown and the match timer; the host collects both rubbing types, sees the full-set reveal and the route, sails to the final island's claim tile and holds E for ten seconds; both browsers show the results with the host as the winner.
